A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPELA, with matching core concepts and retained MNIST-family evaluations. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A and B are included in this assessment.

before.justification: V1 reports original noisy-Boolean classification, MNIST-family evaluations, representation visualizations and one-epoch few-shot results in Section 3.

after.justification: V2 reports original SPELA(O) benchmark, learning-dynamics, few-shot, transfer-learning and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix B, alongside attributed results from prior work.

M1.justification: V2 introduces SPELA(O), changing layer-first training into an epoch-first traversal that updates successive layers as each sample moves forward, avoiding redundant passes through preceding layers (Section 3.3, Algorithm 1). The written training loss also changes from log(2 − cosine similarity) to negative cosine similarity.

E1.justification: V2 removes the noisy AND/OR/XOR evaluation while retaining MNIST, KMNIST and Fashion MNIST. It adds direct CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN evaluations, plus ResNet50-based transfer learning on Aircraft-100, CIFAR-10, Flowers-102 and Pets-37 (Section 4.3, Appendix B).

E2.justification: V1's experimental comparator is BP. V2 adds accuracy comparisons with FA, DRTP and PEPITA using explicitly attributed published scores (Tables 3 and 7), and adds binarized BP in Table 6. PEPITA's earlier appearance in v1 Table 1 was an algorithm-property comparison, not an accuracy evaluation.

E3.justification: The few-shot comparison changes from one epoch with a 784-200-100-50-15 SPELA network to five epochs with a 784-1000-34 SPELA(O) network; BP architectures and learning rates also change. V2 adds matched-versus-tuned BP learning-rate controls, five-versus-100-epoch comparisons, and top-1/top-5 transfer-learning protocols (Figure 4, Table 4, Appendix B.2).

E4.justification: V2 adds Euclidean-loss, random-embedding and weight-binarization ablations, network-width allocation analysis, learning dynamics, and weight-distribution/QQ comparisons (Section 4, Appendix B.1). V1's three-dataset SPELA-versus-BP t-SNE analysis is replaced by a MNIST before/after-training analysis.

E5.justification: V1 already reports means and standard deviations in Table 3 and three-trial averages in Figure 4. V2 explicitly specifies five runs for key evaluations and adds shaded standard-deviation bands (Figures 2 and 5, Table 4). This refines reporting without establishing that unchanged experiments received additional runs.

E6.justification: V1 Table 3 reports one-epoch MNIST accuracies of 92.99% for SPELA and 32.61% for BP at its reported 0.99 split; v2 Table 4 reports 94.69% and 80.59% under its five-epoch, 99%-test protocol. These are replaced results under different conditions, not same-setting gains. Extensive benchmark, transfer and ablation results are added, while Boolean results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds operation-count and activation-memory complexity analysis for SPELA, SPELA(O) and BP, specifying equal-width layer assumptions and excluded memory costs (Section 3.4, Table 2). V1's mathematical projection argument for dispensing with bias (Section 2.2) is removed.

C1.justification: V2 drops prominent claims about modeling perceptual learning, solving XOR with two output neurons, and consistently outperforming BP after one epoch. It introduces SPELA(O), transfer-learning capability and analytical efficiency bounds as central contributions, with stronger emphasis on resource-constrained learning.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly disclaims complete biological plausibility, explains redundant computation in the original schedule, and qualifies its memory analysis. It adds explanations of tolerance to random embeddings and limitations of transfer-learning advantages by dataset, training-set size and accuracy metric (Sections 3.3–4.4, Appendix B.3).

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds ResNet50 feature-extraction instructions, transfer-network dimensions, and a 50-epoch training budget with learning rate 0.001. Conversely, v1's MDS-based cross-layer embedding construction and explicit batch-size settings are no longer specified. These are changes in technical documentation as well as additions supporting new experiments.

R1.justification: V2 substantially shifts positioning from perceptual neuroscience toward on-device learning and alternative training algorithms. It adds work including TinyTL, SymBa, self-contrastive forward-forward learning and graph forward learning, identifies PEPITA as the closest approach, and removes much of v1's perceptual-prior and speed–accuracy-tradeoff bibliography.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list and closing discussion are extensively rewritten. Background Works becomes a standalone Related works section, methods and experiments are reorganized, and the original training/inference algorithms move to an appendix with revisions.

P2.justification: V2 merges v1's architecture and inference illustrations into a compact two-panel Figure 1, replaces the principal result and t-SNE displays, and adds complexity, ablation and transfer tables. New learning-dynamics, transfer and appendix weight-distribution/QQ panels substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses the original schedule's redundant forward computation and substantially strengthens evaluation through BP learning-rate controls, design ablations and transfer tests. Explicit complexity assumptions and applicability qualifications improve support for the central efficiency argument. Resource savings remain theoretical, and Section 4.4.2 misstates Fashion-MNIST accuracy drops relative to Table 6, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial methodological and evidential gains.
